adventure_pages: One sunny morning, Chichi was walking past a school with his friends, Mina and Joon. He saw a flag flying high above the playground. “What a beautiful flag!” said Chichi. “What is it called?”
“That’s the flag of South Korea,” said Mina. “We call it the Taegukgi!” Chichi looked closely. “I can see red, blue, black and white,” he said. “Do all the colours mean something?”

“They do!” said Joon. “Look at the circle in the middle.” “The red and blue parts represent opposite forces in balance.” Chichi thought for a moment. “So different things can work together?” he asked. “Exactly!” said Joon.

Chichi pointed to the black lines. “What about those funny shapes?” “They’re called trigrams,” explained Mina. “They represent heaven, earth, water and fire.” “Wow!” said Chichi. “There’s a lot more to this flag than I thought!”

Later, the friends visited a history museum. They saw a display about the first Taegukgi. “Korea began using the Taegukgi in the 1880s,” explained Joon. Chichi stared at the old pictures. “That was a very long time ago!”

The next display showed people carrying the Taegukgi during Korea’s struggle for independence. “The flag helped people feel brave and hopeful,” said Mina. Chichi looked at the pictures quietly. “It must have meant so much to them,” he said.

Back at school, the Taegukgi waved proudly in the sunshine. “Today, we see it at schools, celebrations and sporting events,” said Joon. “And on special national holidays!” added Mina. Chichi smiled. “Now I understand why your flag is so important.”

Then Chichi grinned. “Would you like to see the flag from my home?” He pulled out a little flag with a big red dragon. “That’s the Welsh flag!” he announced proudly. Mina laughed. “A dragon! Just like you!” “Of course!” said Chichi. “I’m a Welsh dragon!”
